items.profileType: How do I choose the right profile type?
items.contact: How do public contact settings work?

answers.profileType: Profile type describes how you show up in the public marketplace. Company authority still comes from memberships and permissions, not from the label alone.
answers.verification: Verification explains which public checks Buildink completed. It should never imply guarantees beyond the published verification scope.
answers.contact: Public detail pages should expose only approved contact methods, while sensitive or unapproved contact data stays private.

search.title: Search across the public Buildink marketplace
search.description: Browse companies, people, suppliers, equipment, projects, tenders and open requests from one multilingual discovery flow.

companies.title: Find construction companies with public proof
companies.description: Search by region, category and trust signals to move quickly from public evaluation into the right next action.

profiles.title: Browse public marketplace profiles
profiles.description: Explore the final five profile types with role-aware cards, public proof and privacy-safe contact pathways.

suppliers.title: Explore supplier businesses and approved catalogs
suppliers.description: Public supplier pages should clarify what the business offers, where it operates and how visitors can enquire.

equipment.title: Browse equipment with clear availability signals
equipment.description: Keep equipment discovery scannable with category, condition, availability and provider context up front.

projects.title: Discover public construction projects
projects.description: Public project pages should expose scope, timing, location and public budget rules without leaking private delivery data.

tenders.title: Monitor open tenders and deadlines
tenders.description: Tender listings should emphasize source attribution, date clarity and a clean handoff into protected bidding workflows.

companyRequests.title: Open requests for companies and subcontractors
companyRequests.description: These listings should feel distinct from projects and tenders while still staying structured, indexable and easy to compare.

workerRequests.title: Public workforce requests by trade and region
workerRequests.description: Show trade, quantity, timing and public terms clearly so workers and contractors can decide whether to continue.

serviceRequests.title: Public requests for specialized construction services
serviceRequests.description: Find structured service RFQs without exposing private commercial terms.

workers.title: Find verified workers by trade and region
workers.description: Worker cards should show profession, skills, availability and public verification without private documents.

subcontractors.title: Discover subcontractors ready to bid
subcontractors.description: Compare trade, crew size, service radius and qualification signals before inviting or contacting.

serviceProviders.title: Browse professional construction service providers
serviceProviders.description: See service categories, licences, regions and response signals on a public-safe profile.

trades.title: Explore companies and professionals by trade
trades.description: Start from a trade and move into companies, subcontractors and workers with matching capabilities.

howItWorks.title: How Buildink works for every public audience
howItWorks.description: Explain discovery, verification, posting and response flows before asking visitors to create an account.
howItWorks.sectionOneBody: This page should answer the first practical question every visitor has: what can I do here, and what happens next?

cards.card1Body: Clarify how companies publish public identities, projects, requests and approved contact paths.
cards.card2Body: Show how workers, contractors and service providers are discovered and verified in a public-safe way.
cards.card3Body: Explain how supplier and equipment visibility turns into real enquiries without exposing private data.

verification.title: What Buildink verifies - and what it does not
verification.description: Use plain language to describe public verification meaning, privacy boundaries and how visitors can report concerns.
verification.sectionOneBody: Trust pages work best when they increase confidence without over-claiming what the platform can guarantee.

cards.card1Body: Explain what a badge represents on company, profile and listing pages.
cards.card2Body: Make it clear that private identity and verification files do not belong on the public surface.
cards.card3Body: Visitors should always know how to report unsafe, misleading or incorrect public content.

about.title: About Buildink
about.description: Present the Italy-first marketplace story, the trust model and the practical problem Buildink is solving.
about.sectionOneTitle: A product story grounded in real work
about.sectionOneBody: The About page should feel credible and specific, not like generic startup filler.

cards.card1Body: Show why Buildink exists and which fragmented workflows it is trying to simplify.
cards.card2Body: Speak clearly to companies, professionals, suppliers, equipment owners and project teams.
cards.card3Body: Connect the public website story to verification, privacy and safer professional discovery.

contact.title: Contact Buildink
contact.description: Create a clear route for business, support and general enquiries with privacy-safe contact guidance.
contact.sectionOneBody: Contact pages should feel practical, well-structured and respectful of regional and language differences.

cards.card1Body: Help visitors choose between support, partnerships, marketplace questions and general business enquiries.
cards.card2Body: Surface only approved official address, email, phone and working hours.
cards.card3Body: The public contact flow should validate cleanly and explain what happens after submission.

help.title: Help center
help.description: Lead with task-based support content so public visitors can answer common questions before opening a ticket.

faq.title: Buildink FAQ
faq.description: Keep common marketplace questions concise, scannable and easy to navigate across languages.

blog.title: Blog and insights
blog.description: Publish trustworthy long-form content that supports discovery, trust and multilingual search visibility.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: This page is structured for approved client legal text with clear navigation and update visibility.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.description: Present the approved service terms with the same readability and information hierarchy as the rest of the site.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.description: Explain cookie categories, vendor intent and user controls in a way that stays understandable on mobile.

home.proofTitle: Designed to look credible before a user ever logs in
home.proofBody: The public experience should show real marketplace depth, trust signals and role-specific pathways without exposing private operational data.
